mainTopic: Whether the leftover blood (שירים) is essential to an offering, and the start of the משנה on communal and individual חטאות
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge about squeezing out bird-offering blood (מיצוי), and the גמרא answers that two תנאים reported רבי ישמעאל's view differently. רמי בר חמא then says that a certain תנא holds the leftover blood (שירים) is essential. He quotes a ברייתא that uses the word ״אוֹתָהּ״ to teach that a חטאת whose blood belongs above the red line is invalid if the blood was placed below. The ברייתא tries several logical proofs for this rule, rejects each one, and falls back on the פסוק. רמי בר חמא argues that the ברייתא's phrase 'the inner מזבח does not complete them' refers to the leftovers. רבא answers that if that were so, a simple קל וחומר would have proven the rule without a פסוק, so the phrase must mean the sprinklings on the פרוכת. Next comes a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה read ״וְכִלָּה מִכַּפֵּר״ in opposite ways. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree about whether their dispute is only about how to read the פסוק or about whether שירים are essential. The attempt to prove which אמורא holds which view is rejected. Finally, a new משנה begins the laws of the communal and individual חטאות.

steps.title: End of the challenge: if no blood remains, there is nothing to squeeze out
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a challenge from a ברייתא: what does not remain does not need to be squeezed out, so מיצוי is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if no blood remains, he does not squeeze it out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that began earlier. A ברייתא says that if no blood is left, the כהן does not need to squeeze any out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן can skip squeezing when nothing is left, then squeezing (מיצוי) cannot be essential to the offering. That seems to clash with the view attributed to רבי ישמעאל in the discussion just before.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that does not remain; there is no leftover
It shall be squeezed out (the blood of a bird חטאת pressed out onto the altar)
Squeezing out the blood of a bird offering

phrases.english: And that which does not remain, he shall not squeeze out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun in the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view attributed to רבי ישמעאל about squeezing out the blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If squeezing can be skipped when no blood is left, it is not essential. That contradicts the view treating it as essential.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about רבי ישמעאל's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two תנאים report רבי ישמעאל's opinion differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי ישמעאל held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the two sources do not need to agree, because they come from two different תנאים reporting רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing both sources into one view, the גמרא splits them. One תנא understood רבי ישמעאל one way, and the other תנא understood him differently, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (two different teachers of the משנה period)
According to the view of

phrases.english: There are two tanna'im,
and they disagree according to Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two תנאים (תרי תנאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources reflect one single view of רבי ישמעאל, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source reflects a different תנא's version of רבי ישמעאל's view, so there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: When two sources about one Sage clash, the גמרא can answer 'תרי תנאי': two תנאים reported his view differently.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: this תנא holds the leftover blood is essential
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says a certain תנא holds that שירים are essential, and brings a ברייתא on 'הכהן המחטא אתה'. It teaches that a חטאת is valid only if its blood was put above the red line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: This תנא holds that the leftover blood is essential. As it was taught: 'The כהן who offers it as a sin offering' teaches 'it', the one whose blood was placed above, and not the one whose blood was placed below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רמי בר חמא says that the תנא of a certain ברייתא holds that pouring the leftover blood is essential, and he begins quoting that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word 'אתה' (it) as limiting. Only a חטאת whose blood went above the red line is eaten by the כהן, while one whose blood went below is disqualified. How this shows that שירים מעכבי will become clear as the ברייתא continues.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood after the main sprinklings, poured at the base of the altar
They are essential; leaving them out disqualifies the offering
Above or below (the red line around the middle of the altar)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama says:
This tanna holds that the remainder of the blood is essential.
As it is taught: "The priest that sacrifices it for sin"
"It" means the one whose blood was placed above,
phrases.notes: Above and below here mean above or below the red line that ran around the middle of the altar.

phrases.english: and not the one whose blood was placed below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new line of discussion about the leftover blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא of this ברייתא holds that שירים מעכבי. The ברייתא teaches that a חטאת whose blood was placed below the red line instead of above is disqualified.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether the leftover blood is essential decides if an offering is still valid when the כהן never poured it out.

steps.title: Why would we think blood placed below still works?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק is needed. It answers that since blood meant for four placements still works with one, we might think blood meant for above also works below.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said this, but where would the other idea come from? From the פסוק 'and the blood of your offerings shall be poured on the altar' we learned that offerings needing four placements still bring atonement with just one. So one might think blood meant for above, placed below, also brings atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops to ask why the פסוק needed to teach this at all. It explains the mistaken idea we might have had without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that not every detail of the blood service is essential: four placements can be cut down to one and the offering still works. Based on that, we might think the location (above or below the line) is also not essential. The ברייתא presents this as the possible mistake (יכול).

keyTerms.meaning: Where did you come from? (what made you think otherwise?)
Four placements of blood, one on each corner of the altar
A single placement of blood
He brought atonement; the offering is valid
One might have thought (introduces a mistaken idea)

phrases.english: You said this, but from where did you come?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why would anyone think the offering is valid, so that the פסוק has to say it isn't?

phrases.english: From the fact that it is stated:
"And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out against the altar," etc.
we learned regarding those placed with four placements,
that if he placed them with one placement, he has effected atonement.
One might think that even those to be placed above
that he placed below effect atonement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the derivation from 'אתה' in step 3 is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would we think a חטאת whose blood was placed below is valid, so that the פסוק must exclude it?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since four placements can be reduced to one and still work, we might think a change in location also does not disqualify.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying blood placed below actually works. It is only describing the mistaken idea (יכול) that the פסוק comes to reject.

steps.title: A logical argument: blood for above should not work below
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a דין: blood meant for below does not work if placed above, so blood meant for above should not work if placed below.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is a logical argument: blood was commanded above, and blood was commanded below. Just as blood commanded for below does not bring atonement if placed above, so too blood commanded for above should not bring atonement if placed below!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now offers a logical argument (דין) that seems to prove the rule without needing the פסוק. This sets up the next move, where the ברייתא will test this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood belongs above the line (an animal חטאת) and some belongs below (a bird חטאת). We already know blood meant for below fails if placed above, so the ברייתא compares the two: blood meant for above should likewise fail if placed below. If this argument holds, the פסוק 'אתה' seems unnecessary, which is why it will be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical; introduces a reasoning-based proof
The blood about which it was stated (where the Torah said to put it)
Just as... so too... (the pattern of a comparison argument)

phrases.english: And it is a logical inference: blood is stated above,
and blood is stated below;
just as blood that is stated to be below,
where he placed it above, does not effect atonement,
so too blood that is stated to be above,
if he placed it below, does not effect atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mistaken idea of step 4 with a logical comparison, which seems to make the פסוק unnecessary.
steps.raayaObject: That blood meant for above the red line does not bring atonement if placed below
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to blood meant for below, which does not work if placed above
steps.whyThisMatters: If logic alone proves the rule, the פסוק 'אתה' would be extra. The ברייתא will need to show why this argument is not strong enough.

steps.title: The logic from lower blood is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the comparison. Lower blood never goes above, but upper blood partly goes below anyway, since the leftovers are poured at the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Blood meant for below may fail above because it never ends up above. But blood meant for above does partly go below, so maybe placing it below works.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own comparison from step 5. It shows that the two kinds of blood are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood meant for below has no connection to the upper area at all, so it makes sense that it fails there. Blood meant for above already has a part that goes below (the leftovers poured at the base). So maybe the lower area is acceptable for it, and the comparison falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'lower' bloods, meant for below the red line
The 'upper' bloods, meant for above the red line
It brought atonement (it worked)
Is offered below

phrases.english: No; if you said this about the lower bloods
that were placed with a placement above
that is because they never end up above, so it did not atone;
will you say the same about the upper bloods that he placed below,
when some of them are offered below?!
phrases.notes: He means the leftover blood, which is poured out at the base of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison offered in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between lower blood and upper blood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Upper blood already has a part that goes below, while lower blood has no part that goes above

steps.title: The inner blood is brought as a new proof
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings the blood that is sprinkled inside the היכל as a new proof. Some of it is offered outside, yet if it was placed outside first, it does not atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The inner blood proves the point. Part of it is offered outside, but if he put it outside from the start, it did not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to fix the broken proof with a new example. The inner blood shows that having a part that goes somewhere does not make that place acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said that since some upper blood goes below, below might be acceptable for it. The inner blood answers that argument. Its leftovers go to the outer מזבח, yet placing it outside first does not work, so the same could be true of upper blood placed below.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood sprinkled inside the היכל
Will prove (a counter-example)
Outside, on the outer מזבח
At the start, before the main placements

phrases.english: The inner blood (leftovers) will prove it –
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'leftovers'.

phrases.english: since some of it is offered outside,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נְתָנָן בַּתְּחִלָּה בַּחוּץ לֹא כִּיפֵּר!
phrases.english: and yet if he placed it outside at the start, it did not atone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 6 with a counter-example
steps.raayaObject: That upper blood placed below should not atone, even though part of it goes below
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of inner blood placed outside at the start

steps.title: The inner blood proof is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The inner blood is different, because the inner מזבח does not finish its atonement and more placements are still needed. Upper blood is finished on the corners, so maybe it is valid below.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The inner blood is not finished by the inner מזבח. But the corners do finish the upper blood, so maybe it is valid if he put it below.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the new proof from step 7. It shows a difference between inner blood and upper blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inner blood still needs further placements after the inner מזבח, so it is a weaker case. Upper blood is fully finished by its placements on the קרנות, so it is a stronger case. A stronger case might be valid even when it is placed below, so the proof does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: Finishes them off, completes their atonement
The inner (golden) מזבח inside the היכל
The corners (horns) of the מזבח
Valid

phrases.english: No; if you said this about the inner blood –
that is because the inner altar does not finish it;
will you say the same about the upper bloods –
when the corners do finish them?
So if he placed them below, they should be valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Inner blood is not completed by its own מזבח, but upper blood is completed by the corners

steps.title: The word ״אוֹתָהּ״ settles it
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot prove it, the פסוק teaches with ״אוֹתָהּ״ that a חטאת is valid only if its blood was placed above, and not if it was placed below.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says ״אוֹתָהּ״, meaning 'it': the one whose blood was placed above is valid, but not the one whose blood was placed below.
steps.whatsHappening: Every logical proof has failed, so the ברייתא concludes that this rule comes from a פסוק. The word ״אוֹתָהּ״ limits validity to a חטאת whose blood went above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This back-and-forth explains why the פסוק is needed. Without it, we might have thought upper blood placed below is still valid. ״אוֹתָהּ״ teaches that it is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
'It', a word that limits the rule to a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת whose blood belongs above the red line is invalid if the blood was put below. Logic could not prove this, so it comes from the word ״אוֹתָהּ״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the end of the ברייתא that רמי בר חמא brought in step 3. It shows that the placement of the blood above the line is required for the קרבן to be valid.

phrases.english: The verse says: "it" –
it, whose blood was placed above, is valid,
but not one whose blood was placed below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 knocks down the last logical proof (the one from the inner blood in step 7), the ברייתא falls back on the פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Blood of a חטאת meant for above the red line is invalid if placed below, as derived from ״אוֹתָהּ״

steps.title: Proof that the inner leftover blood is essential
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא argues that the ברייתא's words 'the inner מזבח does not complete them' must refer to the leftover blood (שירים), which shows that pouring them is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the ברייתא mean when it says the inner altar does not complete them? Isn't it talking about the leftover blood?!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא goes back to a phrase from the ברייתא and uses it as proof for his own view about the leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8 the ברייתא said the inner blood is different because the inner מזבח 'does not complete' its atonement. רמי בר חמא asks what still remains to be done, and answers: the pouring of the leftovers at the base outside. If the atonement is not complete without them, then the leftovers must be essential.

keyTerms.meaning: Completes them, finishes their atonement
The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל
The leftover blood, poured out at the base of the outer מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the whole basis for the claim that the leftover blood of the inner offerings holds up the atonement. רבא's answer in the next steps decides whether that claim stands.

phrases.english: What does 'the inner altar does not complete them' mean?
Is it not these, the leftovers?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שֶׁאֵין מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי מְמָרְקָן? לָאו אֵלּוּ שִׁירַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a phrase from the ברייתא's rejection in Step 8 and uses it to prove רמי בר חמא's opening claim in Step 3, that this תנא holds שירים מעכבי.
steps.raayaObject: That pouring the leftover blood of the inner offerings is essential to the atonement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's phrase 'the inner מזבח does not complete them' (Step 8).

steps.title: If so, the ברייתא could have used a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רמי בר חמא: if the inner leftovers were truly required outside, the ברייתא could have proven its rule by a קל וחומר and would not have needed a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, prove it with a קל וחומר. The inner leftovers must end up outside, yet if the blood was put outside from the start, it does not atone. The blood placed above does not have to end up below. So if it was put below from the start, isn't it logical that it does not atone?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the proof by showing that it leads to a strange result: the ברייתא would have had an easy logical proof and would not have needed the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the inner leftovers are a real requirement outside, the logic goes: even blood that must end up outside fails when it is put outside first. Upper blood has no required ending below, so putting it below first should surely fail. The ברייתא did not use this logic and needed a פסוק (Step 9), which shows that the leftovers are not a real requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
A requirement, an essential obligation
Atoned, made the offering work

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the קל וחומר is correct. He is saying that if רמי בר חמא were right, this קל וחומר would work. Since the ברייתא went to a פסוק instead, רמי בר חמא's reading must be wrong.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If so, derive it with an a fortiori argument:
Just as the inner leftovers,
whose final stage is a requirement outside,
if he did them outside at the start, it did not atone;
those placed above,
whose final stage is not a requirement below,
and he did them below at the start,
is it not logical that it did not atone?!
phrases.notes: Since the ברייתא needed the word אוֹתָהּ (Step 9) instead of this simple logic, the leftovers must not be required.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִי הָכִי, תֵּיתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רמי בר חמא's reading in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim that 'not completing' refers to the leftovers, which would make them essential.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the leftovers were essential, a simple קל וחומר would prove the ברייתא's rule. But the ברייתא used a פסוק, so the claim cannot be right.

steps.title: The phrase really refers to the פרוכת
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a different reading: the inner מזבח alone does not finish the atonement, because blood must also be sprinkled toward the פרוכת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the inner altar does not complete them by itself. The curtain is also needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes knocking down the proof by giving the ברייתא's phrase a new meaning that has nothing to do with the leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Does not complete' does not mean that something must still happen outside. It means the inner מזבח is not the only place blood goes inside; there are also sprinklings toward the פרוכת. So the phrase gives no proof that the leftover blood is essential.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain between the היכל and the קודש הקדשים
Alone, by itself

steps.whatToRemember: רמי בר חמא tried to prove from the ברייתא that the inner leftovers are essential. רבא showed that this would make the ברייתא's פסוק unnecessary, and explained 'the inner מזבח does not complete them' as referring to the sprinklings on the פרוכת, not to the leftovers.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵין מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי מְמָרְקָן בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: Rather, the inner altar alone does not complete them,
but rather the curtain is also needed.
phrases.notes: He means blood is also sprinkled toward the curtain inside, so the inner altar is not the only stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵין מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי מְמָרְקָן בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא פָּרוֹכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing in Step 11 that רמי בר חמא's reading cannot be right, רבא supplies the correct reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רמי בר חמא's proof from the ברייתא entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'does not complete' was assumed to mean the leftovers, but it really refers to the additional sprinklings on the פרוכת.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא reads the verse: if he atoned, he finished
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes ״וְכִלָּה מִכַּפֵּר״ and brings רבי עקיבא's reading: once the atonement is done, the service is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "And when he has finished atoning." If he atoned, he has finished. If he did not atone, he has not finished. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא about the פסוק describing the end of the כהן גדול's blood service on יום כפור. רבי עקיבא explains what 'finished' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, 'finished' depends on 'atoned.' Once the placements that bring atonement are done, the service counts as complete. This sets up the reading that רבי יהודה will flip in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "And when he has finished atoning" (ויקרא 16:20)
He atoned, meaning he did the blood placements that bring atonement
He finished

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And when he has finished atoning"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:20. This is about the כהן גדול on יום כפור.

phrases.english: if he atoned, he has finished,
and if he did not atone, he has not finished.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא that connects to the earlier discussion of the inner blood and its leftovers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: the service is finished once the atoning placements are done.

steps.title: רבי יהודה flips the reading: if he finished, he atoned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks why we should not read it the other way: only if he finished everything did he atone, so missing one placement means nothing was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Why don't we say, if he finished, he atoned, and if he did not finish, he did not atone? Then if he left out even one of all the placements, he did nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה challenges רבי עקיבא's reading and offers the opposite one. His version makes every placement essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא made 'finishing' depend on 'atoning.' רבי יהודה makes 'atoning' depend on 'finishing.' Under his reading, if even one placement is missing, there is no atonement at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Why should we not say? This introduces a different reading.
The blood placements (sprinklings) on the altar
He has done nothing at all

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him,
For what reason do we not say:
if he finished, he atoned,
if he did not finish, he did not atone?
So that if he left out one of all the placements,
he has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא with the opposite reading of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק can just as easily be read the other way, which would make every placement essential.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what actually changes between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It is setting up the next step, where two אמוראים explain the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that a missing placement means no atonement. So the גמרא wants to know whether their disagreement has any practical result.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical result comes from the two readings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halachic difference between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Two answers: only how to read the verse, or whether the leftovers are essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One says the dispute is only about reading the פסוק. The other says it is about whether שירים are essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One says the only difference between them is how to read the meaning of the verse. The other says the difference between them is whether the leftover blood holds back the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question, and the גמרא does not yet say who said which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: there is no practical difference at all, only two ways of reading the פסוק. Answer two: there is a real difference. For רבי יהודה, the leftover blood (שירים) must be poured or the offering fails. For רבי עקיבא, it does not hold back the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: How to read the meaning of the פסוק, with no practical difference
The leftover blood poured at the base of the outer מזבח after the placements
Hold back, meaning they are essential and without them the offering fails
One says

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us here which אמורא holds which view. The next steps try to figure that out.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי;
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree:
One says:
the meaning they read into the verse is the difference between them,
and one says:
whether the leftovers hold back the offering is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי; חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the difference is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One אמורא: only a dispute about reading the פסוק. The other: a dispute about whether שירים are essential.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the leftovers view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who says the dispute is about שירים, because elsewhere he speaks about 'the one who says שירים מעכבין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that it is רבי יהושע בן לוי who says the difference is that the leftovers hold back the offering. For רבי יהושע בן לוי said: According to the one who says the leftovers hold back the offering, he brings one bull and starts again from the beginning inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove which אמורא holds which view. It brings another statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי mentions an opinion that שירים מעכבין, and he rules that if the blood was lost before the leftovers were poured, a new bull must be brought and the inside placements redone. Since he speaks about such an opinion, the גמרא assumes it is this ברייתא, and that he is the one who sees the dispute as being about שירים.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude, or let it be settled. This introduces a proposed proof of who said what.
According to the one who says
Bull, here the bull offering of the כהן גדול on יום כפור
Inside, meaning on the inner מזבח inside the היכל

phrases.english: Conclude that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
is the one who says the difference is that the leftovers hold back the offering;
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
According to the one who says the leftovers hold back the offering,
he brings one bull,
phrases.notes: This is the case where the blood spilled before the leftovers were poured on the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: and starts from the beginning inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to identify which אמורא gave the second answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who says the dispute is about שירים מעכבין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling, 'According to the one who says שירים מעכבין, he brings one bull and starts again inside.'

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן also speaks about this view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבי יוחנן also mentions 'the one who says שירים מעכבין,' so the proof does not tell us who is who.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say רבי יוחנן does not hold this reasoning?! But רבי יוחנן said: רבי נחמיה taught in line with the one who says the leftovers hold back the offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from the last step. רבי יוחנן also refers to someone who holds שירים מעכבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that only someone who speaks about a 'שירים מעכבין' opinion could be the one who sees this ברייתא as being about שירים. But רבי יוחנן also speaks about such an opinion, through רבי נחמיה. So his statement shows the same thing, and the proof cannot decide between the two אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? This introduces a rhetorical challenge.
He does not hold this reasoning

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yochanan
does not hold this reasoning?!
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Rabbi Nechemya taught
in line with the one who says the leftovers hold back the offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֵית לֵיהּ הָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Weakens the proof given in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that identified רבי יהושע בן לוי as the 'שירים מעכבין' explainer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן also refers to an opinion that שירים מעכבין, so mentioning that opinion does not single out רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Both אמוראים Were Speaking Generally, So the Proof Fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its pushback. When רבי יוחנן said 'the one who says שירים מעכבין,' he meant whoever holds that view, not רבי עקיבא or רבי יהודה specifically. The same is true of רבי יהושע בן לוי. So neither statement tells us who said what.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was speaking about 'whoever holds that view,' not about these particular תנאים. Here too, he was speaking about 'whoever holds that view,' not about these particular תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rejection of the proof from step 17. Both רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי were speaking in general terms, so neither line proves which of them explains the argument as being about שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 tried to prove that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who ties the argument to שירים, because he mentioned 'the one who says שירים מעכבין.' Step 18 noted that רבי יוחנן said the same phrase. Now the גמרא explains why that cancels the proof: each was quoting the view in general, not linking it to the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words of the one who says, meaning whoever holds that view
The תנאים, the teachers of the משנה era (here: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה)
Here too, meaning the same explanation applies to the other case

steps.whatToRemember: The proof was rejected. We still do not know whether רבי יוחנן or רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who says the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה is about שירים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא decided who holds what. It only showed that this proof doesn't work, and the question stays open.

phrases.english: Rather, [he spoke] according to the words of the one who says
phrases.notes: This is about רבי יוחנן, who in step 18 mentioned 'the one who says שירים מעכבין.'

phrases.english: and not referring to these תנאים;
here too, according to the words of the one who says
phrases.notes: Now it's about רבי יהושע בן לוי, whose words were used as the proof in step 17.

phrases.english: and not referring to these תנאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר וְלָאו לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the pushback from step 18 by explaining why the phrase in both statements proves nothing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof in step 17 that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who links the argument to שירים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'the one who says' is a general reference to a view. It does not point to the specific argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה, and both אמוראים use it.

steps.title: The New משנה: Communal Sin Offerings and Their Blood
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the communal sin offerings: the goats of ראש חודש and of the festivals. They are slaughtered in the north, their blood is received in a service vessel in the north, and their blood is placed on all four corners of the מזבח. It then asks how this is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: About the communal and individual sin offerings. Which are the communal sin offerings? The goats of ראש חודש and of the festivals. They are slaughtered in the north. Their blood is received in a service vessel in the north. Their blood needs four placements, on the four corners of the מזבח. How is this done?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the rules of the sin offerings (חטאות). It defines the communal ones and gives their basic rules, then asks 'how?' to set up a step-by-step description that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives three rules for these goats: where they are slaughtered (north), where their blood is received (north, in a כלי שרת), and how much blood is placed (four placements on four corners). The word כיצד does not raise a challenge. It opens the משנה's own explanation of how the כהן does the four placements.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal sin offerings, brought for the whole people
The goats brought as sin offerings on ראש חודש
The north side of the Temple courtyard
A sacred service vessel used in the Temple
Placements of blood on the מזבח
The corners (horns) of the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: These rules (north, a כלי שרת, four corners) are the basic picture of a חטאת, and the coming details build on them.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The communal and individual sin offerings:
Which are the communal sin offerings?
The goats of ראש חודש and those of the festivals.
Their slaughter is in the north,
and the receiving of their blood in a service vessel is in the north,
and their blood requires four placements
on the four corners [of the altar].
How [is this done]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the previous one ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The communal sin offerings are the goats of ראש חודש and of the festivals. They are slaughtered in the north, their blood is received in a כלי שרת in the north, and their blood is placed on all four corners of the מזבח.
